title: Libya's Mufti Renews Warning Against Government Power-Sharing Deal With Haftar, Faults Tripoli Cell Probe Delays
detail: Grand Mufti Sheikh Al-Sadiq Al-Gharyani warned the Dbeibah government on Thursday, September 24, 2026 against entering a power-sharing arrangement with Khalifa Haftar — reportedly the US-brokered plan under which Dbeibah would stay prime minister while Saddam Haftar assumes the presidency — cautioning the government could become 'its first victim.' Al-Gharyani accused the government of concealing what he called a 'major conspiracy' orchestrated by foreign states, chiefly the UAE, which he described as 'the claw of the Zionists,' and criticized the Presidential Council for distrusting domestic investigations in favor of international involvement. He separately faulted the Attorney General's office for resolving minor cases quickly — citing the plane crash in Misrata — while investigations into more serious matters, including the Derna disaster and Arkenu Oil Company affairs, saw little progress. On the economy, he addressed unequal wage increases and urged a unified salary scale, subsidy reform, and a crackdown on fuel smuggling by what he termed 'family-run brigades.'

media.caption: Libya's Grand Mufti Sheikh Al-Sadiq Al-Gharyani renewed his warning against a Haftar power-sharing deal, Sep 24, 2026

confidenceReason: Reported directly by Libya Observer with extensive direct quotes attributed to the Mufti's own statement; single-outlet report, consistent with the Mufti's repeated public opposition to the rumored Boulos power-sharing plan documented in this tracker's claims since earlier in 2026.

title: Presidential Council Head Menfi Meets US Adviser Boulos in New York on Institutional Unification, Elections
detail: Presidential Council head Mohammed Menfi met US Senior Adviser for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos at Libya's UN Mission in New York on Thursday, September 24, 2026, on the margins of the 81st UN General Assembly session, to discuss advancing Libya's political process and ending the country's institutional divisions. Menfi welcomed unification efforts including US initiatives, stressing that 'the success of such efforts depends on Libyan ownership of the political process and respect for the laws,' and called for building on existing understandings within a broader national process that expands participation to national forces and institutions. Boulos praised Menfi's role in bridging differences among Libyan parties. Both sides agreed to maintain consultations toward unified institutions and inclusive elections ending the transitional phase.

media.caption: Presidential Council head Mohammed Menfi meets US adviser Massad Boulos at Libya's UN Mission in New York, Sep 24, 2026

confidenceReason: The meeting and both officials' statements are reported directly by Libya Observer across two separate articles (a same-day in-brief and a fuller writeup); both are the same outlet, so this remains a single-source confirmation, though it is consistent with Boulos's broader documented UN General Assembly week of Libya engagement (he also met Haftar and addressed the Security Council on Libya integration steps per LANA reporting).
